FFmpeg from your system's package manager

Helia does not download this. Your package manager downloads and installs FFmpeg from your
distribution's own software repository (or from Homebrew), under that repository's rules. Helia
runs the one command shown, with your permission and nothing else. If the command needs
administrator rights, your system asks you for your password; Helia never sees it.

FFmpeg is free software. Depending on how your distribution built it, it is licensed under the
GNU Lesser General Public License (version 2.1 or later, or version 3 or later) or under the GNU
General Public License (version 2 or later, or version 3 or later). Your package manager shows
the exact licence of the package it installs, for example with `apt show ffmpeg`,
`dnf info ffmpeg-free`, `pacman -Si ffmpeg` or `brew info ffmpeg`. The source code is available
from the same repository and from https://ffmpeg.org/download.html.

Some video formats are covered by patents in some countries. Whether that affects you is a matter
between you and the people who supply the package, not Helia.

Helia is not affiliated with FFmpeg or with your distribution.
